clue.text: Complain, and a student gives a bit of a hand

parts.note: to carp is to complain or grumble
L is the learner driver's plate, so a student

explanation.surface: Someone who grumbles and then, with a student, lends a little help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives a bit of a hand' reads as helping out; it is the definition, a bone of the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpal bones form the wrist, which is part of the hand, so a carpal is one small piece of it.

clue.text: Danger coming from garden, for example

definitions.text: Danger coming from garden, for example

parts.words: Danger coming from garden, for example
parts.note: the letters of danger can be rearranged from garden, and such a reshuffled word is the thing defined

explanation.surface: A warning about a hazard lurking in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: DANGER rearranges GARDEN, and a word made by rearranging another's letters is this kind of word puzzle.

clue.text: Resentment's highest point, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so a word sounding like the highest point is wanted

parts.note: a peak is the highest point, as of a mountain

explanation.surface: Resentment is said to be at its highest.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of irritation from wounded pride is a feeling of being slighted, a mild form of anger.

clue.text: Electioneers sacked after ignoring one city

indicators.note: a place that is sacked is plundered and left in disorder, so the letters are scattered
ignoring means leaving out, so these letters are dropped from the campaigners

parts.note: taken as written, O, N and E

explanation.surface: Campaign workers fired after neglecting a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring' removes O, N, E from ELECTIONEERS, leaving ELECTIERS; 'sacked' rearranges those letters. Leicester is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a large English city in the East Midlands, so an example of an urban centre.

clue.text: Check with pilot for person on board

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
a pilot is an airman, one who flies aircraft

explanation.surface: A flying instructor checks a pilot to find someone to take aboard an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a passenger on a plane; here the board is a company's board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a company's board of directors presides over its meetings, so is a person on the board.

clue.text: Make a large profit from tip in trophy

indicators.note: in puts the tipping word inside the trophy

parts.note: a cup is a sporting trophy
to tip is to lean over

explanation.surface: Making a fortune from a tip-off placed inside a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a betting tip or tip-off; it is a verb meaning lean.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is an idiom for winning or earning a great deal of money in one go.

clue.text: A long letter

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it, to yearn

explanation.surface: A lengthy letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the letter but is a verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the eighth character of the alphabet, H, as it is spoken.

clue.text: Water is mostly ice on Loire, apart from the banks

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ice can mean coolness of manner, reserve

indicators.note: a river's banks are its edges, so the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A river described as frozen except along its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice' is not frozen water here but coldness of manner, RESERVE; 'mostly' drops its final E. The Loire is a French river, so 'banks' fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a large stored body of water, typically an artificial lake supplying a town.

clue.text: Crime waves among drivers in this country

indicators.note: among places one piece inside another

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is the British motoring organisation for drivers

indicators.note: a crime wave sets the word in motion, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crime wave among motorists somewhere in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waves' signals the rearrangement of CRIME; 'drivers' are the AA, Britain's Automobile Association, the motoring breakdown service.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points to a particular nation, the United States, so this phrase stands for that country.

clue.text: Got time, having served teas, for such a thing as Marmite?

parts.note: to have got something is to have acquired it

indicators.note: teas that are served are dished out, so the letters of the word are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Someone finds time to serve tea and asks whether Marmite would go with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmite is a salty yeast spread famous in Britain for being loved or hated; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmite is the classic example of a flavour people must grow to like, which is what this phrase means.

clue.text: Refiner working with energy and no constraints

indicators.note: a refiner at work is busy, and the word's letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An oil refiner works energetically with no limits imposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' sends the letters of REFINER plus E into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Having full freedom to act as one pleases, like a horse given a loose bridle, means being without restraints.

clue.text: Fearless in command, chasing the girl's love

indicators.note: a piece that chases another comes after it, so this one is placed at the end

parts.note: her is the possessive for a girl, 'the girl's'
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
IC is the abbreviation for in charge or in command, as in 2IC

explanation.surface: A brave officer pursues the woman he loves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heroic shows great courage, acting without fear in danger.

clue.text: Rogue deed and its consequence?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal or rogue
a deed is an act, something done

explanation.surface: A wicked act and the fallout that follows from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The effect or influence that follows from an action is its result, so these are near synonyms.

clue.text: A vile tale about moderate

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters of these words are reordered

explanation.surface: A nasty story concerning a moderate politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like a noun describing a person but is a verb meaning ease.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate pain is to lessen or ease it, which is to moderate it.

clue.text: Quietly spoken — by a good man of the countryside

indicators.note: by means beside, so the spoken piece sits next to the good man

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
ST, saint, is a good man in crossword usage
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken good man of rural parts, perhaps a country vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a pastor, but the definition is the adjective at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes rural life, shepherds and fields, so it means belonging to the countryside.

clue.text: In the manner of a servant that's wasteful, cloaked in cunning

definitions.text: In the manner of a servant

indicators.note: cloaked in means wrapped inside, so the wasteful word goes inside the cunning one

parts.note: sly means cunning or crafty
lavish means extravagant or wasteful

explanation.surface: A wasteful servant hiding behind cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something slavishly means doing it with servile obedience, as a slave or menial would.

clue.text: Ducks walk when crossing road

parts.note: a mall is a sheltered walk or promenade, like London's Mall

indicators.note: one piece crossing another lies over it, so here it holds the other inside

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Ducks waddling across a road.
explanation.definitionFit: The commonest wild duck has this name, so the plural is a group of birds of that kind.

clue.text: Spray a wild rose and look up

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the letters run riot
in a down clue up means the piece reads bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: Spraying a wild rose and glancing upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' turns ROSE into EROS; 'up' turns LO into OL.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised can that releases its contents as a fine mist, a spray.

clue.text: Quantity of fire if fuel oddly absent?

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job

indicators.note: with the odd letters absent, only the even letters are kept

explanation.surface: A puzzle over how much fire there would be without fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like flames but means dismiss. Dropping the odd letters of 'if fuel' leaves FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sackful is the amount a sack holds, so a measure or amount of something.

clue.text: Such clues must be a burden

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden or trial

explanation.surface: A solver grumbling that the horizontal clues are a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the clue itself, which is one of the horizontal set in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: This clue sits in the horizontal list of the puzzle, so it is one of that type of clue.

clue.text: Let off after satirical piece becomes target for bowler

indicators.note: after places the rearranged word behind the satirical piece

parts.note: a skit is a short satirical sketch

indicators.note: off means awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A satirical sketch is let off, then aimed at a cricket bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges LET into TLE. The bowler here is a player at ninepins, not cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A skittle is one of the wooden pins a bowler aims to knock down in the game of skittles.

clue.text: Fearful Catholic's first inhabitant of the Tower

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: ravens famously live at the Tower of London

explanation.surface: A frightened Catholic was the first prisoner held in the Tower.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tower of London keeps a colony of ravens; legend says the kingdom falls if they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A craven person is cowardly, lacking courage, so frightened or timid.

clue.text: Changes to Venice, apart from the west end, seen as relative

indicators.note: changes made to a word alter the order of its letters
in a word read left to right, the west end is the first letter, which is left out

explanation.surface: Visiting Venice, apart from its western quarter, as a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apart from the west end' drops V from VENICE, leaving ENICE; 'Changes to' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, so a family member.

clue.text: Double feature offering cheers

indicators.note: double asks for the piece to be written twice

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A cinema showing two films offers a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double feature' reads as two films in one programme, but feature is a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old-fashioned toast said when raising a glass, the same as saying good health.

clue.text: Distance one propels a bicycle

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length of 22 yards, the length of a cricket pitch
the linked loop from pedals to back wheel drives a bicycle

explanation.surface: How far a single rider pedals a bike.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a surveyor's length of 22 yards and the looped metal links driving a bike's wheel share this name.

clue.text: Ultra-modern nation frequently needing courage

parts.note: a state is a nation
oft is an old word for often
heart means courage, as in 'take heart'

explanation.surface: A modern country that often needs bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing the most advanced technology available, this phrase means the very latest, cutting-edge.

clue.text: Unhappy with ring and flower

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad or unhappy
to give someone a bell is to ring them by telephone

explanation.surface: A sad person with a wedding ring and a bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring woodland plant with drooping bell-shaped blooms, so a kind of bloom.

clue.text: New Yorker's talk about name and borders of Eire

indicators.note: about means around, so the talk wraps the name

parts.note: to yak is to chatter or talk

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An American chatting about names and the Irish frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for any American, especially a northerner; New York's baseball team also bears the name.
